$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

F1 race: process.rs:80 spawn starts the child immediately, and assignment can only happen after process.rs:80-86 returns. std::process::Command exposes no hook between creation and resume. CREATE_SUSPENDED (process.rs:78 already uses creation_flags for CREATE_NO_WINDOW) needs the primary thread handle to ResumeThread, which std does not return; closing the race needs toolhelp thread enumeration or NtResumeProcess, i.e. more unsafe code. The stream emits SessionStart hook_started/hook_response before any user message (fixtures README:62-68), so child processes at startup are plausible.

F2 sync vs async: commands.rs:40-41 pick_project is pub async fn (comment at :39). commands.rs:53 list_projects, :58 start_session, :63 list_sessions, :68 list_inbox, :73 answer, :88 stop_session are sync pub fn. Tauri docs (v2.tauri.app/develop/calling-rust) say commands without async run on the main thread.

F2 writer: process.rs:47-54 send_line locks the stdin Mutex and calls write_all/flush on the calling thread. No channel, no writer thread. Callers: mod.rs:184 (inside start, no Sessions lock held) and mod.rs:267 (inside send_through, after the Sessions lock is released at :266). The blocking write holds the calling thread, not the Sessions lock.
F2 tokio: tokio 1.53.2 is in Cargo.lock via tauri v2.12.2 (cargo tree -i tokio). Not a direct dependency in Cargo.toml.

F2 contract: ipc.ts:114-127 invokes start_session and answer with {args: ...}. Tauri docs say an async command invoked from JS already returns a promise and works like any other command, so argument names and JSON shape do not change. Caveat from the same docs: async commands cannot take borrowed args such as the State type with a lifetime unless they return Result. start_session and answer already return Result, and pick_project already does (commands.rs:41-44). Making them async alone would still block a tokio worker during the write, so the write itself must move (writer thread, or spawn_blocking).

F3 ordering: mod.rs:163 let summary = session.summary(); captures status Starting (state.rs:127 in SessionState::new). mod.rs:172 calls the spawner, which starts the reader thread (process.rs:92). mod.rs:181-183 stores proc. mod.rs:184 send_line. mod.rs:196 fires the captured summary (status Starting) outside any lock, and mod.rs:197 returns the same stale value. Meanwhile the reader can apply Init (state.rs:203-211, Starting to Working) and fire via on_output (mod.rs:201-214). Events are computed under the lock but fired after release (mod.rs:211-213), so re-reading under the lock at :196 does not fix emit order; a sequence number would be a contract change in types.ts.

F4 ordering: mod.rs:252-273 send_through. mod.rs:264 let line = f(&mut s.state, now_ms())? mutates state under the lock before the write. state.rs:296-304 reply() resolves Finished and Error items and sets Working. state.rs:263-279 and :281-294 (answer_permission, answer_question) call close_pending (resolves the item) and recompute before returning the line. mod.rs:267-270: on send_line error, proc.kill() and return Err with no fire. The item stays resolved and status Working until the reader Exit arrives, then state.rs:325-334 mark_exit sets Failed (non-zero) or Ended (0) and pushes an error item. The state.rs:262 doc comment says State changes only on success, which does not hold on this path.

architect.rationale: Diamond, 3 slices, all parallel off b38ae28. Disjoint file sets: s1 = src-tauri/src/session/process.rs + NEW src-tauri/src/session/process/job.rs (declared from process.rs as a child module, so mod.rs is not touched) + Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock; s2 = src-tauri/src/session/mod.rs + state.rs + protocol.rs + src-tauri/src/commands.rs; s3 = desktop/src/App.tsx + state.ts + state.test.ts + components/InboxItemView.tsx + NEW src/reply.ts + NEW src/reply.test.ts. No file appears in two slices. The overlap the scout flagged (process.rs by F1/F2/F6, mod.rs by F2-F5) is removed by fixing F2 with spawn_blocking in commands.rs instead of a writer thread in process.rs, so process.rs belongs only to s1 and mod.rs only to s2. Freeze that makes them independent: the Proc trait (send_line, kill) and the signature of process::spawn do not change; the s2 Fake and the s1 ProcessHandle both keep implementing the same trait. Each done_when runs on its own branch from b38ae28. The change carries new unsafe Win32 code and lock-ordering logic, so it is not one to merge unreviewed. Diamond over single-loop because review cost differs by slice: s1 and s2 need a high-effort reviewer, s3 does not. Risk tags: s1 HIGH because it adds unsafe FFI, a new direct dependency and a Cargo.lock edit, and the crash path (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE when the app dies) is invisible to cargo test. s2 HIGH because the fixes are lock-ordering and race logic (emit order, a per-session send gate, commit after write), and a test can show the ordering it scripts but not the absence of a deadlock. s3 LOW because it is pure reducer and helper logic fully covered by vitest, with no sensitive data and no shared file.

decisions.F1: Option (a): assign the job after spawn, accept the race and document it, with a direct Windows-only dependency windows-sys version 0.60 with features Win32_Foundation, Win32_Security, Win32_System_JobObjects and Win32_System_Threading, under the cfg(windows) target dependencies table. Feature gates were verified against the local windows-sys-0.60.2 source. CreateJobObjectW needs Win32_Security, and JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION needs Win32_System_Threading. Cargo resolves to the locked 0.60.2, so there is no download and no new package entry. Why the race is acceptable: the window is the few microseconds between CreateProcess returning and AssignProcessToJobObject. Before claude.exe can create a child it must load its JS runtime and reach the SessionStart hook, which takes milliseconds or more, so a grandchild cannot realistically exist inside the window. (b) was rejected. Raw CreateProcessW means re-implementing pipes and argument quoting in unsafe code. The variant that keeps std (CREATE_SUSPENDED, then a Toolhelp thread walk and ResumeThread) leaves a suspended orphan if resume fails. Both cost more unsafe code than the race costs. That variant is recorded as the upgrade path if manual check M1 ever finds an escaped grandchild. (c) was rejected because win32job is unverified and crates.io is unreachable. (d) was rejected because the leak is real today. Semantics: one Job per session, created with null security attributes, so the handle is not inheritable and the app holds the only handle. JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE is set through SetInformationJobObject(JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation). When the last handle closes, every process in the job is terminated. That covers the paths that run no code: a crash, a panic under the panic=abort release profile, and Task Manager killing the app all make the kernel close the app's handles, so the job closes and the whole tree dies. RunEvent::Exit and kill_all no longer carry this alone. Breakaway is not allowed (neither BREAKAWAY_OK nor SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK), so descendants stay in the job. Windows 8+ nested jobs mean assignment still works when the app itself runs inside a job, for example under a terminal or an IDE. The Job lives in ProcessHandle (an owned wrapper whose Drop calls CloseHandle), so it lives exactly as long as the session's Proc. kill() calls TerminateJobObject, then the existing child.kill() as a fallback. If CreateJobObjectW or AssignProcessToJobObject fails, the session still starts with job = None and the current behavior, and the failure is never surfaced as an error string containing a path. All unsafe code is confined to process/job.rs, and every unsafe block carries a SAFETY comment.
decisions.F2: spawn_blocking, not a writer thread. start_session and answer become pub async fn returning Result<_, String>: clone the Arc<Sessions> out of State and run the existing synchronous call inside tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking (verified present in tauri-2.12.2 src/async_runtime.rs:311). A JoinError maps to a short string with no path. Why not a writer thread: an enqueue returns before the write happens, so a write failure would arrive asynchronously, and F4 needs it synchronously to decide whether to commit. spawn_blocking keeps send_line synchronous on a blocking-pool thread, so the main thread never blocks and no tokio core worker is used. JS invoke contract identical: same command names, same args shape, same return types. Async commands taking State are legal because both return Result. stop_session and the list_* commands stay sync because they never do I/O while holding a lock (kill is non-blocking, see s1). Consequence handled in s2: commands can now run concurrently, so two answers to one item could both build a line. s2 adds a per-session send gate.
decisions.F5: Surface only. Write nothing back. protocol.rs gains Message::UnsupportedControlRequest with request_id and subtype. state.rs pushes an Error inbox item (summary along the lines of: Claude sent a request Orchestra cannot answer (<subtype, truncated to 64 chars>). The session may be waiting; stop it if it does not continue.), leaves the status unchanged and does not increment unknown_count. Why not answer with an error control_response: that shape (subtype error, request_id, error) is not in any s1 fixture. A live check is not cheap, because Orchestra sends no initialize, so it registers no hooks, SDK MCP servers or callbacks, and there is no known way to make the CLI emit a non-can_use_tool request to test against. Sending an unverified shape risks the CLI rejecting or exiting on it. Surfacing fixes the actual harm, a session silently stuck in working with no inbox item, without depending on an unverified shape. Answering stays a follow-up gated on a fixture that records one.
decisions.F3: Emit order is guaranteed by an emit lock, not a contract change. Sessions gains emit_order: Mutex<()>. Every publish computes its events under the Inner lock, takes emit_order while still holding Inner, drops Inner, fires, then drops emit_order. Lock order is always Inner then emit_order, and the emit callback must never call back into Sessions (documented at the field; the lib.rs callback only calls handle.emit). start() no longer fires the pre-spawn summary. After a successful send it re-reads the summary under the lock and publishes it in order, and the return value is that same fresh summary. The UI ignores the start_session return value (NewSession.tsx:21), so it cannot overwrite a newer event either.
decisions.F4: Build-then-commit. state.rs splits each answer into a read-only builder (taking &self, returning the line plus a commit token) and a commit (taking &mut self). permission_line, question_line and reply_line validate exactly as today and mutate nothing. commit_answer(item_id) closes the item only if it is still pending, and recomputes only while the session is in a waiting state and not over. commit_reply(token) resolves only the Finished and Error item ids captured at build time, and sets Working only if nothing was applied since the build. The token carries a per-state epoch that apply and mark_* bump. mod.rs send_through: take the per-session send gate (an Arc<Mutex<()>> stored on Session, cloned out under Inner), build under Inner, drop Inner, write, then on success re-lock, commit and publish. On a write error: kill, return Err, commit nothing, fire nothing. The item stays pending until the reader's Exit makes mark_exit set Failed, which is the honest state. The gate is held across build, write and commit but never together with Inner during the write, so the reader thread, which needs Inner and never the gate, cannot deadlock against a full stdin pipe. Fix the state.rs:262 doc comment so it is true.
decisions.F6: When a job is present, the reader thread reaps with a blocking child.wait() while it holds the child lock. kill() then never needs that lock: it calls TerminateJobObject, then try_lock plus child.kill() as a fallback. When there is no job (job creation failed, or off Windows): the poll stays but backs off from 50 ms, doubling to a 1000 ms cap, and kill() keeps the current blocking lock, which the poller releases between tries. The non-Windows backoff is not the ideal fix. Mac and Linux are CI-only targets per orchestra/CLAUDE.md, and a pid-based kill would need a libc dependency, which is out of scope.
decisions.F7: send() returns Promise<boolean> (true on success). The reply button clears the text only after a successful send, through a small pure helper replyThenClear(send, answer, clear) in src/reply.ts, so it is testable without a DOM library (none is installed and none is added).
decisions.F8: Merge the snapshot instead of overwriting, with no contract change. sessions-loaded merges by id: an existing session is kept when its last_activity_at is >= the loaded one, and sessions missing from the snapshot are kept. Every Rust state change sets last_activity_at = now_ms, so it is monotonic per session. On a tie the existing (event) copy wins. That is ambiguous only within one millisecond, and is documented. A new inbox-loaded action merges as a union by id with resolved = a.resolved OR b.resolved. Items are append-only and resolution is monotonic, so this merge never regresses. App.tsx:49 dispatches inbox-loaded. inbox-updated (the event, the full current list) still replaces wholesale.

not_doing: No change to the IPC contract (no sequence number or rev field on events). F3 and F8 are fixed without one.

No race-free CREATE_SUSPENDED spawn (option b). It is the recorded upgrade path if M1 ever finds an escaped grandchild.
No killing of a session's leftover grandchildren when claude exits on its own with code 0. The job lives until stop or app exit. Noted as a possible follow-up; it is not one of the review findings.
No pid-based kill or libc dependency for non-Windows reaping; the non-Windows path gets only the capped backoff.
No writer thread and no change to the Proc trait.
No DOM testing library (jsdom, @testing-library); F7 is tested through a pure helper.
No edits to protocol/, mobile/, fleet/, tauri.conf.json, capabilities/, lib.rs, ipc.ts or types.ts.
No fix for the pre-existing ghost Starting session a snapshot could show if spawn fails mid-load.
No update to the stale line in orchestra/CLAUDE.md that says no tests exist yet. It is outside every slice's file set and is a separate one-line chore.

findings.issue: Commit db92f0f is authored and committed as 'user.email <nathanjcurtis3@gmail.com>', not the owner identity njcurtis3. Cause: orchestra/.git/config gained a local [user] name = user.email (mtime 2026-10-09 22:28:34, six seconds before s2's commit a725e23 at 22:28:40, which carries the same bad name). Global user.name is njcurtis3. Merging followups-s1 as-is writes a non-owner author into orchestra history, which the constitution forbids ('the author is always the owner'). The last violation cost a history rewrite. Fix: `git -C orchestra config --unset user.name`, then `git commit --amend --reset-author --no-edit` on followups-s1 (and the same on followups-s2). The integrator's merge commits would inherit the bad name too until the config is fixed.

The two `unsafe impl Send/Sync` carry 'Sound because' comments instead of SAFETY:, which keeps gate (d)'s 'unsafe {' and SAFETY: counts equal. The argument itself is real and correct. A job HANDLE has no thread affinity, and Assign/Terminate/Query are thread-safe kernel calls. CloseHandle runs only in Drop, which needs exclusive ownership, so no call can race it. Not gaming in effect, but gate (d) is mis-specified: its regex `unsafe {` does not match `unsafe impl`. Next time make the gate count every `unsafe` item, or label these SAFETY: and accept the mismatch with a note.

closing_the_job_kills_the_tree asserts only that cmd.exe is reaped within 5 s of drop(job). That does prove kill-on-close fired, because ping -n 30 would otherwise keep cmd alive about 29 s. It never checks that the grandchild ping.exe died. Grandchild death is asserted only in the terminate test (ActiveProcesses == 0). Tree death on close holds only by inference: both processes were confirmed in the job, and close kills the whole job. A tighter test would check the ping pid's exit after the drop.

In the test helper tree(), if assign() fails the assert panics. The child (cmd plus ping) is not in any job, so it leaks for about 29 s. This happens only on a test failure, and only for a single run.

findings.issue: F3 guarantees the order of emit calls, but not the order of delivery, on one path. Sync commands run on the main thread. In tauri-runtime-wry-2.12.1 src/lib.rs:263, send_user_message evaluates the event script at once when called on the main thread, but posts it to the event-loop proxy from any other thread. So a reader event that was computed and emitted before stop, and is still queued, reaches JS after stop's Ended summary and resolved inbox. The last-writer-wins reducer then briefly shows the stale Waiting* status and unresolved items. It repairs itself: kill leads to reader EOF, and Output::Exit always publishes afterwards (publish is unconditional), which restores Ended. Not a blocker. Making stop_session async would route its emit through the proxy and close the gap.

F5 behaves as planned: an unanswered unsupported control_request leaves the status unchanged (typically Working) indefinitely, and the Error item text is the only signal. The text is bounded (subtype truncated to 64 chars) and contains no path. Nothing is written to stdin, and unknown_count is untouched.

Behavior change outside races: Commit::Answer now recomputes the status only when it is Waiting*. Suppose a Result left the status Idle with requests still pending, and a reply then set it to Working. Answering one of several leftover requests now leaves the status Working, where the old code recomputed it to Waiting for the next request. This is arguably more correct, since the turn has moved on. Fixtures are unaffected.

The test relies on a 50 ms sleep inside the Fake write to make the two threads overlap. It cannot fail falsely, but if the threads did not overlap, an implementation without the gate would pass. Acceptable.

locks.Inner: Reader thread takes it only inside on_output (via sink), never while holding the child lock: the wait() guard is scoped to the `if has_job` block and drops before sink(Output::Exit). stop() releases Inner inside publish() before calling kill(). kill_all() clones procs under Inner, releases, then kills. send_through never holds Inner across send_line.
locks.emit_order: Always taken after Inner (publish), Inner dropped, emit fires, released. emit is Tauri handle.emit, which does not call back into Sessions. Not held across any process.rs call.
locks.gate (per session): Taken only in send_through, held across send_line and the failed-write kill(). Neither stop(), kill_all(), on_output() nor Drop takes it, so a writer stuck under the gate cannot hold off stop or app exit.
locks.ProcessHandle.child: With a job: the reader holds it for the whole blocking wait(), and its only other user (kill's fallback branch) is unreachable because kill() returns after job.terminate() whenever self.job is Some; has_job and self.job derive from the same attach_job result. Without a job: reader holds it only for try_wait() between capped-backoff sleeps, so kill()/Drop get it within one poll.
locks.ProcessHandle.stdin: Taken only by send_line. Not taken by kill, Drop or the reader.

paths.stop_session: Inner -> emit_order -> release -> kill() -> TerminateJobObject; takes no lock the waiting reader holds.
paths.s2 failed-write kill: send_through -> proc.kill(); production spawner is process::spawn (lib.rs:23), so proc is ProcessHandle and kill() is s1's job.terminate(). Holds only the gate; stdin guard already released when send_line returned.
paths.app exit: RunEvent::Exit -> kill_all() -> job.terminate() per session, lock-free; on crash KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE covers it.
paths.Drop: ProcessHandle::drop -> kill() -> job.terminate() (lock-free), then the Job field drops and CloseHandle also kills. Last Arc<ProcessHandle> lives in Session.proc; the reader holds only Arc<Mutex<Child>>, never the handle.
paths.send_line under gate vs terminated child: A write blocked on a full pipe holds gate+stdin; stop()/kill_all() need neither, terminate the job, the pipe read end closes and write_all returns an error; send_through then calls kill() again (idempotent on an empty job) and releases the gate. Does not block forever.

seam_s1_x_s2.residual_not_red: Unblocking a stuck write relies on every holder of the child's stdin read end dying. A grandchild spawned in the documented spawn-to-assign window (job.rs header) or any grandchild in the no-job fallback could, if it inherited stdin, keep a blocked write pending. Same exposure existed at b38ae28 for all grandchildren; s1 strictly narrows it. Not a new seam defect.
